answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly across the whole swarm: when k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated way, pairwise evidence triggers penalties scaling as O(k²), deducted from their collateral escrows. Detection also applies asymmetric capital depreciation, so controlling a larger sybil swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss rather than merely dividing risk among identities. A lotus, marble, or beacon may label an identity, but none exempts its bond from enforcement.
